subject: physics
question_text: Two vectors have magnitudes P and Q. What are the maximum and minimum possible magnitudes of their resultant?

verification.note: PREDICTED — Session 89 enumeration sweep (archetype × object grid over the NCERT chapter): this question has not appeared in any paper or source book we hold, but the chapter contains it and the 2-mark/4-mark format admits it. Authored as a lean card; promote to a full card when a paper season or a Telangana IPE teacher validates the cell. Split invented, as everywhere.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The rule
lines: For two vectors at an angle θ,
R changes with θ only through cos θ,
and cos θ runs from +1 down to −1.
steps.why: One formula covers every case; the two results are simply its end points.
common_mistakes: Adding the magnitudes directly at any angle.

recall.must_convey: That R is the root of P squared plus Q squared plus 2PQ cos theta, and cos theta runs from plus 1 to minus 1.
accept: root P squared plus Q squared plus 2 P Q cos theta
cos theta from plus one to minus one
reject: P plus Q is the maximum

steps.label: The two limits
lines: Every other angle gives a value between
steps.why: Same direction adds, opposite direction subtracts — the two limits a student can quote without touching the formula.
common_mistakes: Writing the minimum as P − Q and getting a negative magnitude; it is the modulus.

recall.must_convey: That the maximum is P plus Q at zero degrees and the minimum is mod P minus Q at 180 degrees.
reject: cos theta runs from plus one to minus one
